thought.text: The fork commented out the `terms_of_service` validation (which normally defines the accessor) but the seed still assigns it. I'll add the accessor.

reasoning_content:
In upstream, `validates :terms_of_service, acceptance:` - Rails acceptance validation adds an attr_accessor? Actually acceptance validation defines the attribute accessor automatically if it doesn't exist? No... Actually ActiveModel's acceptance validator does define a reader? Hmm, actually Rails' `validates_acceptance_of` adds an attr_accessor for the attribute on the model via `attr_accessor(attribute)` if not defined. Yes! `validates acceptance` uses `attr_accessor` internally. So upstream it works because validator is active. In the fork, the validation is commented out, so no attr_accessor, hence unknown attribute error when assigning terms_of_service.

The seed file passes `terms_of_service: "1"`. The fork commented out the validation but didn't update the seed. This is a bug in the fork.

I should fix by adding attr_accessor :terms_of_service to the User model, or remove it from seed. Minimal change: add `:terms_of_service` to attr_accessor in user.rb. Let me do that.

Actually adding to model is cleaner and matches intent. Let's add.

action.command:
cd /workspace; python3 - <<'PY'
p="app/models/user.rb"
s=open(p).read()
old="  attr_accessor :skip_password_validation, :use_redeemable_code, :login"
new="  attr_accessor :skip_password_validation, :use_redeemable_code, :login, :terms_of_service"
assert old in s
s=s.replace(old,new,1)
open(p,"w").write(s)
print("patched")
PY
grep -n "attr_accessor" app/models/user.rb
